title: Chapter 62 — Contract Pricing, Net Terms, and Credit
intro: Holding pricing under pressure and managing receivables.

sections.title: Pricing Discipline
sections.content:
Contract pricing is agreed upon upfront. Holding it under pressure — when a competitor undercuts or a buyer pushes — is a discipline. If you discount outside the agreement, you signal that the agreement does not matter.

Net terms and credit create risk. Know your store's credit policies. Monitor receivables. Address late payments early — before they become bad debt.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating contract pricing, ask:

Is the salesperson holding agreed pricing — or caving under pressure?
Are receivables being monitored and addressed?
Does the account pay on time — and if not, is it being managed?
